The administration directly launched and operationalized the SAVE student-loan plan, including protected income, interest protections, and earlier forgiveness for some low-balance borrowers (E031). Federal policy and outreach also contributed to substantial Marketplace enrollment, although sole presidential causation is not established (E032). The federal government mobilized rapidly for the Maui disaster through a presidential declaration and agency deployment (E056), but later oversight identified a FirstNet service failure affecting response effectiveness (E057). These positive, ruler-attributed actions coexist with major welfare pressures: Medicaid unwinding created substantial disenrollment risk (E033), homelessness increased to its highest reported level since 2007 (E034), Supplemental Poverty Measure and child poverty rose even as the official poverty rate fell (E035), and severe racial maternal-mortality disparities persisted (E037). Education attendance improved but remained highly adverse in many states (E038).
